Chats grew 32 per cent that year. The US$59m is what the extra chats would have cost without AI — not money saved on the actual bill.

The filings settle the headcount question. The same filing also shows why a claimed saving needs checking. The same annual filing claims about fifty-nine million dollars of AI cost savings. Yet in that same filing, the customer service bill actually rose by four million dollars. Both are true. The bill went up because the company handled thirty-two per cent more chats. The fifty-nine million is what those extra chats would have cost without AI. It is a saving against a bigger bill that never arrived, not cash in the bank. A claimed saving and a smaller bill are different things. Ask which one you are being shown.
